#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the hybrid e2e tests directly, bypassing the VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID
# CTest gate. Drives tests/*.sh against pre-built artifacts in this
# workspace.
#
# Env overrides:
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64 (default: build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64)
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so (default: qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so)
#   VSIM_BIN     sim_<cpu> (default: first sim_* under verilator/build/)
#   FILTER       regex; only run tests whose name matches
#   MODE         csr | pc | both  (default: both) - drives TRIGGER_MODE
#                for round-trip fixtures. Negative drivers run once
#                regardless because they assert orchestrator failure
#                modes orthogonal to the trigger mechanism.
#   JOBS         parallel job slots (default: min($(nproc),
#                free(/dev/shm)/256MB)). Each Tier-2 slot uses a 128 MB
#                /dev/shm mmap and runs 3 processes (qemu1, vsim, qemu2);
#                the headroom check leaves margin for that plus QEMU's
#                own scratch. Pass JOBS=1 for sequential semantics.
#   LOG_DIR      where per-test logs land (default: mktemp -d under /tmp)

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
VSIM_DIR="$ROOT/verilator"
HARNESS="$ROOT/tests"
TEST_DIR="$ROOT/tests/fixtures"

VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
if [[ -z "${VSIM_BIN:-}" ]]; then
  VSIM_BIN=$(ls "$VSIM_DIR"/build/sim_* 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)
fi

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m[skip]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

require() {
  if [[ -z "$2" || ! -e "$2" ]]; then
    fail "$1 not found: $2"
    fail "build artifacts first: 'source ./setup.sh'"
    exit 1
  fi
}
require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul
  # icount_spin: CSR-less spin loop. Used by switching-mode demos
  # T3/T4/T5/T7 (icount, BBV emit, slice-consume, SimPoint loop).
  icount_spin
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip EXPECT_RC=3"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
  "rt_no_qemu_binary|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_no_qemu_binary.sh"
  "rt_gdbstub_timeout|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_gdbstub_timeout.sh"
  "rt_pty_handback|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_pty_handback.sh"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  csr|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of csr|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
    if [[ "$shm_free" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$shm_free" -gt 0 ]]; then
      shm_cap=$((shm_free / 256))
      (( shm_cap < n && shm_cap >= 1 )) && n=$shm_cap
    fi
  fi
  (( n < 1 )) && n=1
  printf '%d\n' "$n"
}
JOBS="${JOBS:-$(default_jobs)}"
[[ "$JOBS" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$JOBS" -ge 1 ]] \
  || { fail "JOBS must be a positive integer (got: $JOBS)"; exit 1; }

FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

LOG_DIR="${LOG_DIR:-$(mktemp -d -t e2e-XXXXXX)}"
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
RESULTS_FILE="$LOG_DIR/results.tsv"
LOCK_FILE="$LOG_DIR/lock"
: > "$RESULTS_FILE"
: > "$LOCK_FILE"

# run_one MODE NAME CMD INDEX TOTAL
# Captures the test command's stdout+stderr into $LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log,
# emits one atomic progress line, and appends a TSV row to $RESULTS_FILE
# (mode<TAB>name<TAB>status<TAB>rc<TAB>elapsed). flock on $LOCK_FILE
# serializes the progress write and the results-file append so concurrent
# children (introduced by the parallel-execution commit) cannot interleave
# their TTY writes or corrupt the tally file.
run_one() {
  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"
  local log="$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log"
  local start end elapsed status rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  set +e
  bash -c "$cmd" >"$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  set -e
  end=$(date +%s)
  elapsed=$((end - start))
  case $rc in
    0)  status=PASS ;;
    77) status=SKIP ;;
    *)  status=FAIL ;;
  esac
  (
    flock 9
    case "$status" in
      PASS) ok   "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (${elapsed}s)" ;;
      SKIP) warn "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=77, ${elapsed}s)" ;;
      FAIL) fail "[$idx/$total] ${name}[${mode}] (rc=$rc, ${elapsed}s) -> $log" ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\n' \
      "$mode" "$name" "$status" "$rc" "$elapsed" >> "$RESULTS_FILE"
  ) 9>"$LOCK_FILE"
}

# Build the workplan: one entry per (mode, name, cmd) tuple. Order
# matters: csr-mode tests first, then pc-mode, then negatives (matching
# the original sequential layout so logs are streamed in the same order).
declare -a WORKPLAN=()
for tm in csr pc; do
  [[ "$MODE" != "both" && "$MODE" != "$tm" ]] && continue
  for entry in "${RT_TESTS[@]}"; do
    rt_name="${entry%%|*}"
    env_prefix="${entry#*|}"
    [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$rt_name" =~ $FILTER ]] && continue
    cmd="TRIGGER_MODE=$tm $env_prefix bash $HARNESS/e2e.sh"
    WORKPLAN+=("$tm|$rt_name|$cmd")
  done
done
for entry in "${NEG_TESTS[@]}"; do
  neg_name="${entry%%|*}"
  neg_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$neg_name" =~ $FILTER ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("neg|$neg_name|$neg_cmd")
done
for entry in "${DEMO_TESTS[@]}"; do
  demo_name="${entry%%|*}"
  demo_cmd="${entry#*|}"
  [[ -n "$FILTER" && ! "$demo_name" =~ $FILTER ]] && continue
  WORKPLAN+=("demo|$demo_name|$demo_cmd")
done

TOTAL=${#WORKPLAN[@]}
step "logs: $LOG_DIR  jobs: $JOBS  mode: $MODE  tests: $TOTAL"

# FIFO-based bounded job pool. Each child reads one token from $SEM_FIFO
# before starting and writes one back on exit; only $JOBS tokens exist,
# so at most $JOBS children run concurrently. Opening the fifo in
# read-write mode (<>) means writes never block the parent. The fifo
# inode is unlinked immediately after fd 8 is bound -- the kernel keeps
# the pipe alive as long as fd 8 is open.
SEM_FIFO="$LOG_DIR/sem.fifo"
mkfifo "$SEM_FIFO"
exec 8<>"$SEM_FIFO"
rm -f "$SEM_FIFO"
for ((sem_i=0; sem_i<JOBS; sem_i++)); do
  printf '.\n' >&8
done

i=0
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  i=$((i+1))
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_cmd="${w_rest#*|}"
  read -r -u 8 _tok
  (
    run_one "$w_mode" "$w_name" "$w_cmd" "$i" "$TOTAL"
    printf '.\n' >&8
  ) &
done
wait
exec 8>&-

declare -A MODE_PASS=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0 [demo]=0)
declare -A MODE_FAIL=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0 [demo]=0)
declare -A MODE_SKIP=([csr]=0 [pc]=0 [neg]=0 [demo]=0)
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()
while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_mode r_name r_status _r_rc _r_el; do
  case "$r_status" in
    PASS) MODE_PASS[$r_mode]=$((MODE_PASS[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    SKIP) MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]=$((MODE_SKIP[$r_mode]+1)) ;;
    FAIL) MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]=$((MODE_FAIL[$r_mode]+1));
          FAILED_NAMES+=("${r_name}[${r_mode}]") ;;
  esac
done < "$RESULTS_FILE"

# Stream failed-test logs in workplan order so the user sees a
# deterministic post-run failure dump.
for w in "${WORKPLAN[@]}"; do
  w_mode="${w%%|*}"
  w_rest="${w#*|}"
  w_name="${w_rest%%|*}"
  w_status=$(awk -F'\t' -v m="$w_mode" -v n="$w_name" \
                 '$1==m&&$2==n{print $3; exit}' "$RESULTS_FILE")
  if [[ "$w_status" == "FAIL" ]]; then
    echo
    echo "=== FAIL log: ${w_name}[${w_mode}] ==="
    cat "$LOG_DIR/$w_mode--$w_name.log"
  fi
done

echo
csr_p=${MODE_PASS[csr]} csr_f=${MODE_FAIL[csr]} csr_s=${MODE_SKIP[csr]}
pc_p=${MODE_PASS[pc]}   pc_f=${MODE_FAIL[pc]}   pc_s=${MODE_SKIP[pc]}
neg_p=${MODE_PASS[neg]} neg_f=${MODE_FAIL[neg]} neg_s=${MODE_SKIP[neg]}
dem_p=${MODE_PASS[demo]} dem_f=${MODE_FAIL[demo]} dem_s=${MODE_SKIP[demo]}
total_pass=$((csr_p + pc_p + neg_p + dem_p))
total_fail=$((csr_f + pc_f + neg_f + dem_f))
total_skip=$((csr_s + pc_s + neg_s + dem_s))
step "summary: csr ${csr_p}p/${csr_f}f/${csr_s}s  pc ${pc_p}p/${pc_f}f/${pc_s}s  neg ${neg_p}p/${neg_f}f/${neg_s}s  demo ${dem_p}p/${dem_f}f/${dem_s}s  total ${total_pass} passed, ${total_fail} failed, ${total_skip} skipped"
if (( total_fail > 0 )); then
  fail "failures: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Switching-mode demo runner: sequentially exercise every M1-M8 mode
# end-to-end via the labeled demo scripts under
# verilator/tests/hybrid/demo_*.sh.
#
# Each demo prints its own banner + per-mode PASS/FAIL line. This
# wrapper adds a final tally and propagates a non-zero exit if any
# demo fails. SKIPs (artifacts missing) do not fail the overall run.
#
# Env (auto-detected from repo layout if unset):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   FILTER        regex; only run demos whose name matches
#
# Usage:
#   bash demo.sh                       # all demos
#   FILTER=simpoint bash demo.sh       # just T4 + T7
#   FILTER='csr|pc' bash demo.sh       # T1 + T2

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
VSIM_DIR=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$VSIM_DIR/.." && pwd)
DEMO_DIR="$VSIM_DIR/tests/hybrid"

export VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
export VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
export VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-$VSIM_DIR/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
FILTER="${FILTER:-}"

# Ordered demo list. Each entry: <id>|<demo-script>
DEMOS=(
  "T1|demo_csr_oneshot.sh"
  "T2|demo_pc_oneshot.sh"
  "T3|demo_icount_roundtrip.sh"
  "T4|demo_bbv_profile.sh"
  "T5|demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh"
  "T6|demo_archive_replay.sh"
  "T7|demo_simpoint_loop.sh"
)

cat <<EOF
============================================================
Hybrid Sim Switching-Mode Demo Suite
============================================================
Repo root : $TOP_ROOT
QEMU      : $VSIM_QEMU
Plugin    : $VSIM_PLUGIN
vsim      : $VSIM_BIN
Filter    : ${FILTER:-<none>}
============================================================
EOF

PASS=0; FAIL=0; SKIP=0
declare -a RESULTS=()
START_TS=$(date +%s)

for entry in "${DEMOS[@]}"; do
  IFS="|" read -r ID SCRIPT <<<"$entry"
  if [ -n "$FILTER" ] && ! echo "$SCRIPT" | grep -qE "$FILTER"; then
    continue
  fi
  printf "\n--- %s : %s ---\n" "$ID" "$SCRIPT"
  if [ ! -x "$DEMO_DIR/$SCRIPT" ]; then
    printf "  MISSING: %s\n" "$DEMO_DIR/$SCRIPT"
    RESULTS+=("$ID  $SCRIPT  MISSING")
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    continue
  fi
  bash "$DEMO_DIR/$SCRIPT"
  RC=$?
  case "$RC" in
    0)  PASS=$((PASS + 1)); RESULTS+=("$ID  $SCRIPT  PASS") ;;
    77) SKIP=$((SKIP + 1)); RESULTS+=("$ID  $SCRIPT  SKIP") ;;
    *)  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); RESULTS+=("$ID  $SCRIPT  FAIL(rc=$RC)") ;;
  esac
done

END_TS=$(date +%s)
ELAPSED=$((END_TS - START_TS))

printf "\n============================================================\n"
printf "Demo Suite Summary  (elapsed %ds)\n" "$ELAPSED"
printf "============================================================\n"
for line in "${RESULTS[@]}"; do
  printf "  %s\n" "$line"
done
printf "  ----\n"
printf "  PASS=%d  FAIL=%d  SKIP=%d\n" "$PASS" "$FAIL" "$SKIP"

if [ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

Kernel modes (measure one region you choose):

- **PC mode**: ELF symbols `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc` (or any `--roi-start`/`--roi-end` symbol/address) resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed.

Whole-program modes (sample by instruction count):
- **icount mode**: single boundary on each leg - plugin `icount=N` fast-forwards QEMU1, vsim `--hybrid-icount M` measures the window and drains. No markers, no warmup; for CSR-less workloads.
- **SimPoint-driven mode**: profile the run into slices, cluster representative phases, measure each phase like icount, weight-combine into a whole-program cycle estimate (`./hsim estimate`). The bbv-profile / slice-consume / archive / replay machinery are its stages, not separate modes.

`TRIGGER_MODE=csr|pc` selects the kernel modes (via `tests/e2e.sh` / `./hsim run`); `./hsim run --mode icount` and `./hsim estimate` drive the whole-program modes. Each yields a cycle figure: kernel/window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`); SimPoint reports the weight-combined `estimated_cycles`.

### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)

`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the handback path. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

### 4.2 PC mode - markerless GEMM, whole-kernel boundary from ELF

Same workload as CSR mode, but the binary carries **no** trigger markers and
the switch PCs are computed at demo launch by reading the ELF.

```sh

```

The demo runs `rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf` - the **markerless twin** of the GEMM
fixture, built `-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -DGEMM_REPEAT=200` from the same source as
the marked `rt_c_v_matmul`. `tests/lib/kernel_roi.sh::derive_kernel_roi` reads
the symbol address of `vmatmul_kernel` (function entry) from `nm` as
`ROI_START`, and disassembles `main` to locate the `jal vmatmul_kernel`
call site - the address of the instruction immediately following it becomes
`ROI_END`. Both triggers are one-shot (QEMU plugin `exit(200)` on first
match; vsim drains on first match), so the measured window is **exactly one
full `vmatmul_kernel` call** (16 outer rows + inner k-loop + vse32 stores),
regardless of `GEMM_REPEAT`. The cycle count should land near CSR mode's
~22808.

The mechanism is fully general - pc mode can target **any** symbol or raw
address. Override either boundary:

```sh

```

Under `tests/e2e.sh` the same knobs are the `ROI_START` / `ROI_END` env vars
(each a symbol name or `0x` address). No fixture plants `_hybrid_*_pc` labels
any more, so PC-mode callers must pass explicit boundaries.

604	vsim measures `VSIM_ICOUNT` insns and drains. No warmup window, so the cycle
605	figure (window cycles = vsim `mcycle` - QEMU `mcycle`, offset 624) includes
606	a cold cache/pipeline at vsim entry.

622	plugin's CSR matcher stays live, so a `csrwi 0x7C0,0` would drain at the marker
623	before the icount target is reached.

639	Real programs are too long to cycle-simulate end to end. SimPoint samples:
640	profile the run into fixed slices, cluster them into a few representative
641	phases, measure each phase like icount mode, then weight-combine into a
642	whole-program cycle estimate. **SimPoint mode is icount mode repeated** at
643	clustering-chosen points. The headline command is `./hsim estimate` (Stage
644	4); the stages below show each piece.

795	
796	| Program size (N_total) | Pick `--slice`  |
797	|------------------------|-----------------|

802	
803	**Picking `--max-k`** (number of phases). Each phase costs **one extra
804	QEMU+vsim drain pair** (~5..10s). SimPoint will sometimes pick fewer
805	phases than `--max-k` if the workload is uniform, so `max-k` is an upper
806	bound, not a fixed count.
807	
808	| Workload structure              | Pick `--max-k` |
809	|---------------------------------|----------------|
810	| Single loop kernel              | 2 (init + body) |
811	| Init + kernel + cleanup         | 3              |
812	| Multi-kernel (e.g. 2 GEMMs)     | 4..6           |
813	| Large benchmark mix             | 8..16          |
814	
815	**Sanity checks after a run.** Read the per-phase rows and apply:
816	
817	1. `BBV rows >= 2 * max_k`. If fewer, drop `--slice` so more rows fit.
818	2. Weights add to ~1.0 and are not all small. If all `--max-k` phases
819	   have similar weights, the workload is uniform and you can drop `max_k`.
820	3. CPIs differ across phases. If every phase reports the same CPI, you
821	   are paying for vsim time without gaining accuracy. Drop `max_k`.
822	
823	**Worked example: gemm.elf** (N_total = 254391):
824	
825	```sh
826	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 5000 --max-k 4
827	# Output:
828	# profile: 4 BBV rows -> .../profile.bb (N_total=254391)
829	# phase K=0 w=0.020 ...   phase K=1 w=0.020 ...
830	# phase K=2 w=0.020 ...   phase K=4 w=0.940 CPI=11.724
831	```
832	
833	`slice=5000` gave only 4 BBV rows -- too few for `max_k=4`. The weights
834	also tell you one phase (K=4, the GEMM kernel) accounts for 94% of the
835	program; the other three are startup. A cleaner setup:
836	
837	```sh
838	./hsim estimate gemm.elf --slice 10000 --max-k 2
839	# slice=10000 -> ~25 BBV rows; max_k=2 -> startup + kernel only
840	```
841	
842	**One-line rule.** Start with `--slice $((N_total/20)) --max-k 2`. Raise
843	`max_k` only when a single dominant phase (w > 0.8) hides sub-phase
844	detail you care about.

907	| Symptom                                                | Cause / fix                                                          |
908	|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
909	| `skip: ... not built; run 'make' ...`                  | `source ./setup.sh` and `make -C tests/fixtures`            |

913	| `vsim drained pc=0x... not in vmatmul_kernel`          | `VSIM_ICOUNT`/`QEMU_ICOUNT` too small (count target lands before the kernel) or wrong fixture for icount mode. |
914	| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
915	| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |

## 6. Common failures and how to read them

| Symptom                                                | Cause / fix                                                          |
|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `skip: ... not built; run 'make' ...`                  | `source ./setup.sh` and `make -C tests/fixtures`            |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                      | Trigger never fired. Wrong mode / wrong PC / wrong icount value.     |
| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                    | `timeout` killed the plugin. Increase `TIMEOUT` or tune the target.  |
| `cannot resolve ROI start/end '<x>'`                   | PC-mode boundary `<x>` is neither a `0x` address nor a defined symbol. Fix `--roi-start/--roi-end` (or `ROI_START/ROI_END`), or use CSR mode. |
| `vsim drained pc=0x... not in vmatmul_kernel`          | `VSIM_ICOUNT`/`QEMU_ICOUNT` too small (count target lands before the kernel) or wrong fixture for icount mode. |
| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |

  | tr -d ':')

# QEMU plugin arg
... -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,enter_pc=$ENTER_PC

---

## 5. SimPoint-driven mode - the whole program

### What it does

Real programs run billions of instructions; you cannot cycle-simulate all
of them. SimPoint samples instead: profile the run into fixed slices,
cluster the slices into a few representative phases, measure each phase like
icount mode, then weight-combine the per-phase cycles into a whole-program
estimate. SimPoint mode is icount mode applied at several clustering-chosen
points.

### Stages

1. **Profile (BBV).** The plugin emits one Basic-Block-Vector row per slice
   of N retired insns into a SimPoint `.bb` file (`bbv_out=`, `slice=N`).
2. **Cluster.** `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint` reads the `.bb` and clusters
   the rows into K representative phases: a `simpts` file (one slice index
   per cluster) and a `weights` file (one weight per cluster).
3. **Per phase.** For each representative slice K: QEMU drains at the end of
   slice K (`slice=N`, `slice_at=K`), vsim resumes and measures that slice's
   cycles (the `mcycle` delta).
4. **Archive / replay (optional).** A drained state plus its shared mmap can
   be packaged into `snap/K/{state.bin, mem, meta.json}` and replayed on
   another host. This is the checkpoint plumbing, not a separate mode.
5. **Combine.** `estimated_cycles = N_total * sum(weight_i * CPI_i)`, where
   `CPI_i = delta_mcycle_i / insns_measured` and `N_total` is the whole
   program's retired-instruction count.

### Cycle figure (the headline)

`hsim estimate` runs every stage and prints the whole-program number:

```sh
./hsim estimate tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --slice 20 --icount 0 --max-k 2
```

Last line:

```
estimated_cycles=<N>  (N=<insns>, weighted_CPI=<x.xxx>)
```

`--icount 0` profiles to program exit, so `N` is the true total
instruction count. Run `./hsim estimate -h` for all flags.

### Stage drill-downs

Each stage also has a standalone demo, useful when debugging one piece:

```sh
# Stage 1+2: profile + cluster
WORKDIR=/tmp/sp-profile bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
# Stage 3: consume one representative slice on vsim
SIMPTS=/tmp/sp-profile/simpts \
  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
# Stage 4: archive a drained state and replay it
WORKDIR=/tmp/sp-archive bash tests/demos/demo_archive_replay.sh
```

### Headline demo: the full loop

`demo_simpoint_loop.sh` chains all stages on `rt_c_v_matmul.elf`:

```sh
WORKDIR=/tmp/sp bash tests/demos/demo_simpoint_loop.sh
```

It profiles, clusters into representative phases, drains each phase, archives
it, and replays each archive on vsim (which finishes naturally on
`csrwi 0x7C0,1`). The loop validates the end-to-end replay chain; use
`hsim estimate` above when you want the whole-program cycle estimate printed.

# Roadmap: run all 7 demos on one RVV GEMM workload

## Goal

Every demo under `tests/demos/` (T1..T7) should showcase its switching mechanism on
the SAME RVV-intrinsic GEMM, so the suite reads as "one workload, the 4 switching
modes": CSR, PC, icount, and SimPoint (shown via its profile / slice / archive /
loop stages, T4-T7). Today demos split between `rt_c_v_regs` and `icount_spin`.

We reuse the existing GEMM `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.c` (16x16x16 outer-product,
`__riscv_vle32` / `__riscv_vmacc_vx` / `__riscv_vse32`).

## Why two builds of one source

`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:471-485`: in icount/slice/bbv modes the default CSR
matcher is STILL registered. A workload containing `csrwi 0x7C0,0` drains AT the
marker and `exit(200)`s before any count target inside the kernel is reached. So:

- Marker-driven demos (csr, pc, archive, simpoint) need the markers -> MARKED build.
- Coun/profile demos (icount, bbv, slice) need a marker-free workload -> MARKERLESS.

Per user decision: one source, a preprocessor macro toggles the markers, built twice.

### Confirmed findings (probed on the built artifacts)
- `nm -n rt_c_v_matmul.elf` -> only `main`, `_hybrid_enter_pc`, `_hybrid_exit_pc`.
  The kernel is inlined at `-O1`, so a PC-range assertion has no symbol to anchor on.
  Fix: mark `vmatmul_kernel` `noinline` (also keeps it in the ROI per
  `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:49-51`).
- Orchestrator CSR-drain is marker-driven: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py:33` passes
  the plugin only `outfile=...`; `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:237` sets replay
  `trigger_kind="csr"`. So T6 and T7 must use the MARKED build.

## Fixture mapping (target state)

| Demo | Mode     | Stage / role           | Build      | ELF                    |
|------|----------|------------------------|------------|------------------------|
| T1   | CSR      | -                      | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T2   | PC       | -                      | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T3   | icount   | -                      | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T4   | SimPoint | Stage 1: bbv profile   | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T5   | SimPoint | Stage 2: slice-consume | MARKERLESS | rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf |
| T6   | SimPoint | Stage 3: archive       | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |
| T7   | SimPoint | headline: full loop    | MARKED     | rt_c_v_matmul.elf      |

T7 keeps current behavior: its small slice/icount targets profile the crt0+init
prefix BEFORE the enter marker (same regime as today's `rt_c_v_regs`); the kernel
runs in the SimPoint replay leg.

---
